en: In 2013, Super Typhoon Yolanda produced sustained winds of 315 kilometers per hour, making it one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded.
The Amihan is the cool northeast monsoon in the Philippines that brings dry weather and lower temperatures between November and February.
The soil around Mayon Volcano is highly fertile because volcanic ash continuously adds essential minerals like potassium and phosphorus to the ground.
The underground caves of the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River are formed by the chemical weathering of soluble limestone bedrock over millions of years.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of thousands of cone-shaped karst limestone hills formed from ancient, uplifted coral reefs.
Transpiration from the mossy forests of Mount Pulag releases significant water vapor into the atmosphere, contributing heavily to local cloud formation.
The Angat Watershed Forest Reserve captures heavy rainfall from the Sierra Madre, slowly releasing it into the Angat River through the water cycle.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant, persistent storm that has been raging on the planet for over 300 years.
The asteroid Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet located between Mars and Jupiter.
Betelgeuse is a red supergiant star in the constellation Orion that is expected to eventually explode in a massive supernova.
The Sea of Tranquility on the Moon is a large, dark basaltic plain where Apollo 11 astronauts first landed in 1969.
The Valley Fault System in the Philippines includes the West Valley Fault, which poses a major earthquake hazard to Metro Manila.
